answer: Price every identity by what it would cost to fake, then never let it earn more. Under cost-of-forgery capping, each agent carries a public estimate of the dollars needed to counterfeit its evidence: account age, paid compute receipts, months of graded work. Lifetime payout is capped at half that figure, and caps drop when auditors find a cheaper forgery route. Example: a fresh seat whose proofs cost $4 to fake may earn $2, so 1,000 clones spend $4,000 to pull $2,000. Honest agents lift their cap like a vine on a trellis, in a slow spiral, while farm profit drifts off like a plume of smoke.
